whatItIs.text: A kidney-shaped variety of the common bean — dark red, light speckled, or white (cannellini) — central to chilli, rajma, and Louisiana's Monday red beans and rice.

historyNote.text: In India the red kidney bean is rajma, in Pakistan surkh lobia, in Jamaica 'red peas' — one bean with a passport of names; canned kidney beans are fully cooked before shipping, which is why they go straight into the pot.

howToChoose.text: Canned, pick undented tins and rinse well; dried, choose glossy unbroken beans and remember red kidney beans must be boiled hard — the FDA's rule is 30 minutes — to destroy their natural toxin.

storage.text: Dried beans keep airtight and dry; soaked or cooked beans refrigerate in their liquid. The rulebook has the cooked-bean window and the never-eat-raw rules.
storage.note: raw and cooked pulse safety lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Cooked kidney beans blend into dips and burger patties, thicken chilli, or roast crisp with chilli powder for snacking.

substitutions.note: softer, earthier; swaps cleanly in chilli
